newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power eases on weather, line return.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power eases on weather, line return.

text.p: U.S. Midwest spot power prices eased Tuesday with the return of exports from the Canadian province of Manitoba and forecasts of cooler weather through much of the U.S. northeast by Wednesday and Thursday, industry sources said.

Manitoba Hydro ceased importing power Tuesday morning and resumed exports to Minnesota and North Dakota after setting up a temporary transmission line in the province to replace two lines taken out in a storm last week.

In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Wednesday were quoted at $18.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the afternoon after trade near $26.00 in the morning, brokers and marketers said.
Next day ECAR power was talked at $28.00-30.00 on Monday.

Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) and Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) on-peak prices also eased, with next-day discussion for MAIN in the $16.00-18.00 range and talk in MAPP at $15.00-17.00, the sources said.
The regions were pegged in the $30.00-32.00 range Monday.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Wednesday delivery was assessed in the $16.00-22.50 range from the $21.00-26.00 range Monday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
